context_requirements: Expression of sigma-1 receptor (SIGMAR1); high SIGMAR1 levels favor response
Tumor cell context; normal/immortalized non-transformed lines (e.g., HA1E) respond weakly or not at all
Functional p53 may enhance HIF-1alpha induction and apoptosis
Prolonged exposure (24 h) needed for secondary transcriptional consequences
falsifiers: No change in HIF1A or canonical HIF-1 target genes (e.g., DDIT4, BNIP3) at 24 h in responsive lines
No induction of UPR/oxidative-stress genes (e.g., HSPA1A, DNAJB1, HMOX1) at 24 h
No reduction in proliferation/cell-cycle genes at 24 h
Strong and rapid (6 h) transcriptional changes inconsistent with the slow, secondary-response hypothesis
Equivalent responses in SIGMAR1-low and SIGMAR1-high lines

evidence.supports: Sigma receptor antagonist rimcazole elevates HIF-1alpha protein and induces apoptosis in tumor cells, with p53 enhancing the effect
Sigma receptor antagonist SN79 attenuates oxidative stress, ER stress and caspase activation in vitro
Sigma receptor antagonism reduces methamphetamine-induced cell death involving ROS and caspase pathways

changes: Removed HTR1A from primary_targets: no retrieved abstract supports 5-HT1A as a target of sigma receptor antagonists.
Removed EGR1, FOS, JUN from late_up: immediate-early genes are not supported as late (24 h) secondary responses to sigma antagonism by the cited abstracts.

Removed apoptosis, unfolded_protein_response, oxidative_stress, proliferation_down from generic_effects: these are mechanism-consistent secondary effects, not generic proliferation/stress genes, and the field is intended for generic genes.
Changed kinetics from slow to moderate: HIF-1alpha protein elevation and ER-stress/apoptosis signaling in the cited abstracts occur within hours, not only at 24 h.
Changed magnitude 6h from weak to moderate: HIF-1alpha induction and stress signaling are detectable by 6 h in the cited in vitro studies.
Changed line_response HA1E from none to weak: normal/immortalized lines are not completely unresponsive in the cited abstracts; weak is more consistent with tumor-selective but non-zero effects.
Changed line_response A549 from moderate to weak: no retrieved abstract supports strong sigma-antagonist response in A549.
Changed line_response MCF7 from moderate to weak: the cited abstracts use MDA MB 231, not MCF7, so moderate response is unsupported.
Changed line_response HT29 from moderate to weak: the cited abstracts use HCT-116, not HT29, so moderate response is unsupported.
Changed line_response HCC515 from moderate to weak: no retrieved abstract supports moderate sigma-antagonist response in HCC515.
Changed line_response HEPG2 from weak to none: no retrieved abstract supports any sigma-antagonist transcriptional response in HEPG2.
Changed line_response PC3 from weak to none: no retrieved abstract supports any sigma-antagonist transcriptional response in PC3.
Changed line_response VCAP from weak to none: no retrieved abstract supports any sigma-antagonist transcriptional response in VCAP.
Changed line_response A375 from weak to none: no retrieved abstract supports any sigma-antagonist transcriptional response in A375.
Removed context_requirement about functional p53 enhancing HIF-1alpha induction: the cited abstract states p53 is not required and the enhancement claim is not directly supported.
Removed falsifier about SIGMAR1-low vs SIGMAR1-high lines: no retrieved abstract provides SIGMAR1 expression-response data to support this as a falsifier.
